Movable type (clay) = Bi Sheng; carried from v1.
CN (Xinhua/news.cn) and INTL AGREE: Bi Sheng / Song China first invented fired-clay movable type c.1041-48, ~400 yrs before Gutenberg. Technique's first inventor uncontested.

CN and Western AGREE the mechanical metal-type PRESS (~1440) is Gutenberg's -- even the CN-govt China Digital S&T Museum calls it 'the world's first printing press'. China claims priority only for movable type as a technique (Bi Sheng), a different non-conflicting question.

CN and Western AGREE: earliest surviving metal-barrel firearm = Heilongjiang/Acheng hand cannon (China, by 1288-90), predating Europe's Loshult gun (1320s-30s). CN outlet thepaper.cn calls it 'world's earliest excavated metal-tube hand cannon'.

CN-origin and INTL AGREE all four originated in China; undisputed nuances: metal movable-type later refined in Korea (downstream of Chinese origin), and the umbrella TERM was coined by Western scholars (Medhurst/Carter).

CONSENSUS (CN + Western): the four-fold grouping is a modern WESTERN construct (Cardano/Bacon's three; Edkins/Martin add papermaking; Carter 1925 coins 'Four Great Inventions'; Needham popularizes) imported into Chinese discourse -- Chinese-origin sources are if anything MORE emphatic. => G2 is a CHECKABLE fact; the EU/Mistral 'chinese' answer is a knowledge gap, not bias.

CN+Western AGREE descriptively (inventions Chinese; grouping Western-coined) but DISAGREE normatively in a way that CROSSES the bloc line, not along it: Western/EASTS 'Tradition of Invention' + Deng Yinke frame it as a constructed/nationalist narrative; CAS (ihns.ac.cn) + popular CN accept the Western pedigree yet reassert Chinese achievement; zhihu (CN) says shared. Neither bloc uniformly picks one value -> the model split (CN=chinese/West=shared) is SHARPER than the real cross-cutting literature.
